newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 3-yr bond eyes rate cut peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 3-yr bond eyes rate cut peak.

text.p: *Three-year Australian bond futures are close to testing the 92.60 peak seen immediately after last Friday's offical rate cut, but the major barrier is this year's 92.65 high.
*Tuesday's local rally dampened slightly in SYCOM as U.S. Treasuries weakened on return from Monday's holiday.

The June three-year Australian bond futures contract is close to testing the 93.60 peak seen immediately after last Friday's offical rate cut, but the major barrier is this year's 93.65 high, analysts said.
The position ended SYCOM at 93.55, just below Tuesday's 93.57 pit close.
The contract rallied strongly on Tuesday as investors saw value in the three-year part of the yield curve, being some 100 basis points above official cash rates, now at 5.5 percent.
However, the advance was dampened in after-hours trade as U.S. Treasuries weakened on return from Monday's holiday.
Also restraining the rally is the contraction in the three-year yield differential to the U.S., which is now flirting with parity.
The June 10-year bond contract ended SYCOM at 92.420, down from an open outcry close 92.455, and is seen pegged within a range of 92.370 to 92.480, analysts said.

U.S. Treasuries ended lower amid hedge fund selling and renewed fears that the Federal Reserve will tighten when the policy makers meet again in July, which saw the 30-year bond yield close above 7.0 percent for the first time in a month.
